extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors, wire-service subscribers, and general news readers
extracted.subtask_description: Conventions and editorial/production metadata used in Associated Press wire stories (datelines, embargo/advance-use markings, bylines, slugs and internal codes) and standard factual reporting/attribution practices for national and international news dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance/embargo instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines such as "ADVANCE FOR USE AT [time] [DAY, DATE]" and corresponding "END ADVANCE FOR USE AT ..." markers appear in stories to specify when copy may be released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP stories carrying an "ADVANCE" tag specify an embargoed release time (example forms in text: "ADVANCE FOR USE AT 7 P.M. EST SATURDAY, FEB. 5", "END ADVANCE FOR USE AT 10:30 A.M. EST SATURDAY, FEB. 5"). Producers must honor those times when distributing or publishing the item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline format
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories begin with a dateline in the form "CITY, DATE (AP)-" (e.g., "WASHINGTON, FEB. 5 (AP)-").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the city, abbreviated month and day followed by the wire source tag "(AP)" and a dash before the lead paragraph; this establishes place and source quickly for editors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and byline conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of bylines and reporter attributions such as "By RUSSELL BRINES", "AP Correspondent FORREST EDWARDS", or simple "(AP) -" after the dateline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the reporter or correspondent and their location where appropriate; attribute quotes and reported facts to named officials or described sources (e.g., "a national defense ministry source said").

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal slugs and story-length or identification codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of editorial metadata and slugs like numeric parenthetical prefixes and codes (examples: "(300) STATE PAPERS", "(240) TWINING", "30.24-577").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These codes function as internal identifiers, length indicators or desk slugs for production and routing; include them in wire copy for editorial processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of concise factual lede
rubrics_metrics.description: Leads promptly state the main fact or development (who/what/when/where/why) — e.g., immediate statements about policy positions, orders, actions, or events in the first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load the most newsworthy elements in a short, direct opening sentence so editors and readers grasp the key point immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of information to official or described sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Where necessary, reports attribute information to officials or unnamed but described sources (examples in copy: "a national defense ministry source said", "a party of U.S. Marines ... was scheduled").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using unnamed sources, describe their position or relation to the information; distinguish between on-the-record named sources and unattributed or described sources to indicate reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quoted material with clear speaker identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct quotations are presented in the text and followed by immediate attribution (for example: "IF WE STOP SHOWING HOW TOUGH WE ARE ..." he said).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place exact quoted language in the story and attribute it to the speaker plus context (title/role) so readers can assess source and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of editorial tags (e.g., (ADVANCE), (WX), location markers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthetical editorial tags like "(ADVANCE)", "(WX)", and location abbreviations appear before or after datelines to signal story type or topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these tags to help desks route copy (weather-related, advance/embargoed material, etc.) and to signal special handling instructions for publication.
